steps.title: Find the area of triangle ABD

lines.text: The diagonal $[BD]$ cuts the parallelogram into two triangles of equal area.

steps.title: Find the area of triangle BCE

lines.text: Triangle $BCD$ is the other half of the parallelogram, so its area is $240\text{ m}^2$.
$E$ is the midpoint of $[CD]$, so $[CE]$ is half of $[CD]$. Triangles $BCE$ and $BCD$ have the same height from $B$, so $BCE$ has half the area.

steps.title: Find two pairs of equal angles

lines.text: $PA \parallel BR$, so $|\angle HBQ| = |\angle HAP|$. Reason: alternate angles.
$|\angle QHB| = |\angle PHA|$. Reason: vertically opposite angles.
Two angles are equal, so $\triangle AHP$ and $\triangle BHQ$ are equiangular, hence similar.

steps.title: Write the ratio of corresponding sides

lines.text: $A \leftrightarrow B$ and $H \leftrightarrow H$, so $AH$ corresponds to $BH$ and $AP$ corresponds to $BQ$.
Corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional: $\dfrac{|AH|}{|HB|} = \dfrac{|AP|}{|QB|}$.
